growth.comment: Derived from AR product revenue; Axis Capital also cites specialty ~-6% and refrigerant gas ~+60% in FY26.

Fluoro: higher volumes across refrigerants, industrial chemicals and fluoropolymers plus better realisations offset raw-material inflation. Specialty: "steady performance despite challenging market"; early signs of agro volume and price recovery in core products.

Chemicals +25% YoY driven by fluorochemicals (higher HFC volumes and realisations, new markets offsetting softer US). Specialty subdued: China overcapacity, pricing pressure; chemicals EBIT margin 25.4% vs 28.9% YoY, entire decline attributed to specialty by Kotak.

srfPosition.fact: HFC capacity to exceed 65,000 tpa after Rs88cr debottlenecking (approved May-2026); plants run at maximum capacity to maximise quota baseline (CY2024-26).
Analyst estimate of SRF R32 capacity ~27,000-28,000 t; management declined to confirm capacity numbers. India domestic R32 demand ~17,000-18,000 t (CMD, Jan-2026).
FY26 refrigerant/fluoro product revenue Rs3,598cr vs Rs2,250cr in FY25 (+60%): "record year in terms of both realizations and volumes".

Anti-dumping duty on R32 imports from China in force ~3 years; sunset review due Dec-2026; CMD says hard to justify as prices are healthy and India pricing independent of ADD. India imposed ADD on R-134a (~Jan-2026) which does not bind as global prices are above the threshold.

US: R32 subject to US tariffs - contracts moved from long-term to consignment-by-consignment; US demand softer (destocking, low-GWP transition); volumes redirected to Middle East and new markets. Middle East shipments disrupted for ~half of Q4FY26 by the regional conflict, recovered in Q1FY27 ("Floron commands differentiated pricing").
Management view: refrigerant demand and pricing to remain broadly stable barring seasonality (Oct-2026); Q2/Q3 weaker than Q1 seasonally.

quotaRegimes.fact: 2026 national HFC production quota 797,800 t; Juhua 299,900 t (37.58%); top six firms ~90% of quota; draft 2027 quota largely keeps 2026 framework; controlled use to fall to 90% of baseline by 1-Jan-2029.

Baseline = average HFC production/consumption of CY2024-26 plus 65% of HCFC-22 2009-10 baseline; freeze from 1-Jan-2028; cuts of 10% by 2032, 20% by 2037, 30% by 2042, 85% by 2047. SRF: CY2027 is a "free year" (anyone with capacity may sell); quotas from 1-Jan-2028 go to 2024-26 producers; MoEFCC 1-Apr-2026 circular requires new capacity to be up by 31-Dec-2027. Government retains right to include HCFC; final view likely early 2027.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for SRF (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: each segment's revenue grows and earns an EBITDA margin (segment EBIT + segment depreciation). Group EBITDA = sum of segments less unallocated corporate costs and forex hedge losses (Screener basis). Valued on sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA by segment), as the street does.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments._why: FY27: Q1 +26% on refrigerant volumes and prices; management guides 15-20% and Q2-Q3 are seasonally weaker for refrigerants. We take 19%. FY28: +12% because calendar 2027 is a "free year" before India's HFC quotas, so new capacity can sell and prices may soften; fluoropolymers (PVDF, Chemours FEP/FKM) start to ramp. FY29: +16% as HFOs (Odisha, Q4FY28) and fluoropolymers run for a full year.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 35.7% in FY26 (EBIT 29.1%); ~33% in Q1FY27 (EBIT 27.6%) as specialty prices stayed under Chinese pressure. We assume no return to FY26's peak: 33.5% / 32.5% / 33.5%.

segments.name: Performance Films & Foil
segments._why: Q1FY27 +42%: the Middle East war shut rival plants and customers panic-bought (management: "an aberration"). We assume Q2-Q4 grow ~10%, so FY27 +18%; FY28 +3% as prices normalise; FY29 +8% from capacitor film, BOPA (Sep-2027), thick BOPET and foil.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 13.2% in FY26 (EBIT 8.8%); ~20% in Q1FY27 (EBIT 17.3%) including low-cost inventory gains. We assume ~12.5% for Q2-Q4 (FY27 14.9%) and 13.5-14% after.

segments.name: Technical Textiles
segments._why: Q1FY27 +28% (belting exports after US tariff cuts, nylon tyre cord, quality-control order on industrial yarn); Q2-Q4 assumed +8%. Mature business: ~5% a year after.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin 13.4% in FY26; ~20% in Q1FY27 including inventory gains. 14% from FY28 (FY22-26 average ~15%).

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated corporate costs and forex hedge losses (reported EBITDA below sum of segments)
assumptions._unallocWhy: FY26: ₹434 cr = ₹188 cr forex losses on long-dated export hedges + ₹246 cr corporate costs. Q1FY27 included a ₹102 cr forex loss. FY27E: the Q1 loss plus ~₹100 cr of corporate costs; FY28-29E assume corporate costs only (~₹150 cr) and no further hedge losses.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 guided ~₹2,500 cr; FY28 carries most of the ₹2,300 cr Odisha HFO plant, BOPA and thick-film lines; Axis expects >₹2,500 cr a year. FY26 actual ₹1,717 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹852 cr ≈ 4.6% of average gross block; H1FY27 ₹452 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt, so no treasury income; other income entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: FY26 other income ₹107 cr before the ₹85 cr Labour Codes exceptional charge; Q1FY27 ₹34 cr.
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 ₹278 cr; Q1FY27 ₹69 cr; debt rising with the capex cycle (₹2,500 cr in FY27).
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 22%; FY26 27% included the exceptional charge; normal ~25%.

dcf._betaWhy: Cyclical chemicals and films; market-like sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Long-run demand for refrigerants, fluoropolymers and films tracks industrial growth; 6% nominal.

dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex intensity falls from ~10-12% of revenue to ~6% once the HFO / fluoropolymer cycle is done.

bull.label: Bull

cover.headline: Refrigerants are carrying SRF while specialty chemicals stall: fairly priced, not a bargain
cover.lead: SRF makes refrigerant gases, chemical building blocks for global agrochemical and pharma companies, packaging films and tyre cord. Chemicals are half of revenue and three-quarters of profit. The record FY26 and Q1FY27 (net profit ₹759 cr, +76%) came from two things: refrigerant prices at a decade high as quotas tighten supply worldwide, and a one-off windfall in films during the Middle East war. Specialty chemicals, the growth engine of FY19-23, has shrunk for two years under Chinese overcapacity. We value SRF the way the street does, on the **sum of its parts: Sep-28E EV/EBITDA, with chemicals at 21x**. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** A P/E cross-check (30x Sep-28E EPS of ₹91.5) lands in the same place; the DCF (₹1,509) warns that cash flows alone support much less while capex runs at ₹2,500 cr a year. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Refrigerants: a quota-protected boom, close to its peak?
arguments.p: Fluorochemical revenue rose 60% in FY26 to ₹3,598 cr. China caps HFC production, cut its R32 exports by ~17,000 tonnes in Jan-Jul 2026 (HSBC), and its R32 price hit a decade high. India's own HFC quotas, from 2028, will be based on 2024-26 output, so SRF runs its plants flat out. But calendar 2027 is a "free year" in which new Indian capacity (~81,000 tonnes of R32 announced, per HSBC) can sell, and UBS and Citi argue prices are near the peak.

arguments.h: Specialty chemicals, the long-term story, is stuck
arguments.p: Specialty revenue fell from ₹4,165 cr in FY23 to ₹3,537 cr in FY26 as Chinese overcapacity cut prices and agrochemical customers ran down stock. In Q1FY27 the chemicals EBIT margin fell to 27.6% from 32.0% in Q4FY26 on specialty pricing. Management says specialty has "scraped the bottom", but expects a "linear and probably slow" recovery; the timing of 6-7 new molecules for innovators is "uncertain at this point, to say it mildly".

arguments.h: Capex: chemicals has earned its money; films has not
arguments.p: Since FY21 chemicals capital rose ₹5,537 cr and earned a 28% pre-tax return on it. Films capital nearly doubled while its profit fell. The next ₹2,500 cr a year goes mainly into HFOs and fluoropolymers, with the pay-off in FY28-29.

arguments.h: Valuation: the market pays ~19x for chemicals
arguments.p: Brokers value chemicals at 18-25x EV/EBITDA. After valuing the other businesses at our multiples, the price implies ~19.0x Sep-28E for chemicals; our 21x leaves ~10% upside. The stock has de-rated from 48x forward earnings (2021-25 median) to ~30.3x FY27E, and fell 8.5% in a day after the Q1 call guided to a softer Q2-Q3.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (late Oct-2026): how far refrigerant prices and the films windfall fade after Q1; any sign of the specialty recovery.
India's HFC quota rules (final view expected early 2027) and refrigerant prices in the 2027 "free year".
Commissioning: PVDF (due end-Sep 2026), Chemours fluoropolymer plants (slipped 3-4 months, ~Q4FY27-Q1FY28), Odisha HFO plant (Q4FY28).
Promoter KAMA Holdings has approval to sell up to 3% by Mar-2027 (so far only a 1.08% transfer to its own subsidiary, Sep-2026).
Sunset review of the anti-dumping duty on Chinese R32 (Dec-2026).

blocks.p: SRF started in 1973 making nylon tyre cord, added refrigerant gases in 1989 and packaging films in 1995, and moved into complex chemicals for global agrochemical and pharma companies from 2004. Today it runs 16 plants in India, Thailand, South Africa and Hungary. Half its revenue is exported. The four businesses look very different on growth, margins and returns, which is why the market values each one separately.

blocks.h: Inside chemicals: two very different businesses

blocks.p: **Fluorochemicals** (₹3,598 cr of FY26 product revenue) are refrigerant gases for air-conditioners, fridges and car ACs, plus industrial chemicals and fluoropolymers. Prices follow a global commodity cycle shaped by regulation: as countries phase down climate-warming HFC gases, supply is rationed by quota, which lifts prices for those who hold quota. **Specialty chemicals** (₹3,537 cr) are custom-made intermediates and active ingredients for global agrochemical (and, increasingly, pharma) innovators. This is a contract business: SRF develops a process for a customer's molecule and supplies it for years. It earns better margins in good times, but it has lost pricing to Chinese makers since FY24 and depends on customers' launch timetables.

sections.title: Refrigerants are rationed by regulation; specialty and films are not

blocks.p: HFC refrigerants are powerful greenhouse gases, so the 2016 Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol makes every country phase them down. That turns a commodity into a quota business: once production is capped, holders of quota earn more. **China**, the largest producer, has capped HFC output since 2024 (797,800 tonnes in 2026, with the top six firms holding ~90%), and its R32 price reached a decade high of ~CNY 63,000 a tonne in 2026. **India** freezes HFC production from 1 January 2028 at a baseline set by 2024-26 output, which is why SRF has run its plants flat out and is debottlenecking to over 65,000 tonnes a year. The catch is **calendar 2027**: a "free year" in which anyone with capacity may sell before the quotas start.

bullets: **Refrigerants.** Q1FY27 chemicals revenue rose 26%: higher volumes in refrigerants, industrial chemicals and fluoropolymers, better prices, plants running at high utilisation and Middle East sales back after Q4's disruption. Management expects refrigerant prices "to stay at current levels or get better" and Chinese prices to hold at least to the end of FY27, but Q2 and Q3 are seasonally weaker than Q1 in both volume and price. SRF will not disclose capacity; analysts estimate ~27-28k tonnes of R32 against Indian demand of 17-18k tonnes, so a large share is exported.

**Specialty.** "Steady", with continuing Chinese price pressure; management sees green shoots in volumes and prices of core products, says the business has "scraped the bottom", but expects a "linear and probably slow" recovery, stronger in H2. 6-7 active ingredients for innovators are ready, but their launch timing depends on customers' registrations: "uncertain at this point, to say it mildly". Pharma is ~10% of specialty; the target is 20-30% by 2030.

**Fluoropolymers.** PTFE is shifting to value-added grades; PVDF (batteries, coatings) was due by end-Sep 2026; two plants built for Chemours (FEP/FKM) slipped 3-4 months on Chemours' design changes and run on a return-on-investment contract.

**HFOs.** The ₹2,300 cr Odisha project (20,000 tonnes of HFOs plus hydrofluoric acid) uses SRF's own non-infringing process and is targeted for Q4FY28; site approvals were still being sought in July. HFOs sell at much higher prices than HFCs. Meaningful volumes would come 8-12 months after start-up, i.e. in FY29.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** SRF's moat is **fluorine chemistry plus regulation**: it can run hazardous fluorination at scale, it owns processes (including a non-infringing HFO route), Chemours chose it as a partner, and India's quota system will lock in existing producers from 2028. That is a genuine, durable advantage. But in **specialty chemicals** China is cheaper and customers choose who makes their molecules; and **films** are a commodity. Two-thirds of the business is therefore cyclical, which is why SRF's ROE swings with the cycle (25% in FY22, 10% in FY25, 14% in FY26) instead of compounding steadily like the best Indian chemical franchises.

sections.title: Six years of growth, two lost years, and now a record half

blocks.p: SRF's revenue rose from ₹4,822 cr in FY17 to ₹14,870 cr in FY23, about 21% a year, as the chemicals business grew from a refrigerant maker into a supplier of complex molecules to global agrochemical and pharma companies. Then the cycle turned. In FY24 revenue fell 12% and net profit fell 38%, and FY25 was weaker still (₹1,251 cr). FY26 was a partial recovery (₹1,835 cr). Q1FY27 was the best quarter in SRF's history: revenue up 32% and net profit ₹759 cr (+76%), helped by strong refrigerant sales and a one-off windfall in films.

blocks.p: Over FY17-26 SRF generated ₹17,438 cr of operating cash and spent ₹15,594 cr on new plants: 89 paise of every rupee. After ₹1,546 cr of dividends there was almost nothing left, so borrowings doubled from ₹2,396 cr to ₹5,083 cr. That is fine if the new capacity earns well. The test is return on capital employed (ROCE): it peaked at 24% in FY22, fell to 12% in FY25 and was 15% in FY26, about SRF's cost of capital.

blocks.callout: **Where it went right and wrong:** split by business, the picture is sharper. Since FY21, capital employed in **chemicals** rose by ₹5,537 cr and its EBIT by ₹1,535 cr: a 28% pre-tax return on the new money. In **films**, capital employed nearly doubled (₹3,425 cr to ₹6,310 cr) while EBIT fell from ₹898 cr to ₹508 cr. Group ROCE fell because of films, not chemicals. CWIP (plants being built) more than doubled to ₹1,889 cr at Mar-2026, and this round of spending is mostly in chemicals (HFOs, fluoropolymers).

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean books, but hedging losses and one-offs to strip out

bullets: **Forex hedge losses.** SRF sells forward its export dollars for long periods. As the rupee weakened, these hedges lost ₹119 cr in FY25, ₹188 cr in FY26 and ₹102 cr in Q1FY27 alone. The company reports them below its own EBITDA; Screener (and this report) treats them as an operating cost. That is why Q1FY27 EBITDA is ₹1,237 cr here and ₹1,373 cr in the company's presentation (which also adds back other income).

**One-offs.** FY26 included an ₹85 cr exceptional charge for the new Labour Codes and a ₹99 cr tax credit from a favourable tribunal order (Q3FY26). Q1FY27 films and textiles margins included low-cost inventory gains that management does not expect to repeat.
**Corporate costs.** Segment EBIT (₹3,008 cr in FY26) is before ₹343 cr of unallocated costs (net of other income). Sum-of-the-parts valuations that ignore this flatter the result; ours deducts it.
**Depreciation before revenue.** New plants are capitalised and depreciated a couple of quarters before they earn. With ₹1,889 cr in CWIP at Mar-2026, depreciation will keep rising ahead of profits.

**Audit.** B S R & Co. (KPMG network) gives a clean opinion; its key audit matter is hedge accounting. It notes that edit logs were not enabled on some accounting master tables during FY26 (a common IT-controls remark).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Segment disclosure is detailed and reconciles to reported profit; the auditor is a Big-4 firm with no qualification. Hedge losses and one-offs are disclosed clearly; investors simply need to strip them out.

sections.title: Moderate debt, working capital rising with sales

blocks.p: Net debt (borrowings less cash and investments) was ₹3,785 cr at March 2026, about 1.1x EBITDA: comfortable for a company of this size. Working capital is the other use of cash. Inventory days (131) and receivable days (59) are high because SRF holds raw materials, refrigerant stock for the cooling season and finished intermediates for global customers. In FY26 inventory rose ₹440 cr and receivables ₹393 cr, faster than sales, and with revenue up 32% in Q1FY27 working capital will need more cash this year.

blocks.p: Of the six broker notes written after the Q1FY27 results, four are Buys (HSBC ₹3,300, IDBI Capital ₹3,604, Motilal Oswal ₹3,200, ICICI Direct ₹3,160), one Hold (Jefferies ₹2,540, upgraded from Underperform) and one Reduce (Prabhudas Lilladher ₹2,482).
